$comment: PreToolUse on Edit|Write, not UserPromptSubmit. §10.4 said UserPromptSubmit, and that was written
before the mechanism existed: UserPromptSubmit receives the user's prompt, which does not name a
file, while the whole briefing is keyed BY file path. PreToolUse is the only event that carries
one. Recorded here rather than silently deviating.
Non-blocking by design: the hook prints the briefing into the transcript. The HALT decision lives
in the pack itself (§10.3's frozen baseline), so a project that has not been governed yet is never
locked out of its own repo on install day.
stderr is NOT suppressed, and `|| true` is what keeps it non-blocking. It used to be `2>/dev/null`,
which meant the three ways a fresh install fails — dependencies never installed, no kg.config.json,
no graph built — all presented identically as the plugin doing nothing at all. Each of those writes
one actionable line saying what to run. A silent failure is the one outcome a briefing hook cannot
afford: it is indistinguishable from a project where everything is governed.
